summary:
Workplace Insight previews the Workspace Design Show London, returning to the Business Design Centre on 24 to 25 February 2027 under a new theme, "The Human Experience of Work." The theme centres wellbeing, inclusion, sensory comfort, belonging, neurodiversity and emotional experience in workplace design, framed against organisations rethinking what makes people want to gather in person. The 2027 edition argues workplaces should move beyond pure functionality toward environments supporting human connection, comfort, mood, acoustics, hospitality and inclusivity.

The theme will shape the whole visitor experience: exhibitor booths, product launches, installations and immersive spaces built with feature partners. Designers, architects, manufacturers and workplace brands will interpret it through original concepts intended to show how design influences workplace culture, productivity and wellbeing.

Confirmed 2027 exhibitors include Brunner, Bisley, Koenig + Neurath, KI Europe, Milliken and Interface. The piece positions the show as the UK's only dedicated platform for workplace interiors, where architects, designers and occupiers source products, meet suppliers, make project decisions and form supplier relationships.

Visitors are promised an expanded exhibition floor, product launches, immersive installations and a content programme on trends and strategies. Returning conference pillars are: Workspace Design Talks (trends and insights on design, strategy and culture); Sustainability Talks (sustainable thinking and initiatives); Occupiers Forum, offering "The View from HQ" on how employers create engaging, high-performing workplace experiences; and FIS: Interiors Insight Live, covering the finishes and interiors sector.

The Workspace Design Awards also return in 2027, judged exclusively by corporate occupiers, developers and project managers, recognising projects with real-world impact. Key dates and entry information are to be announced.

The article is promotional in tone and contains no data, survey findings or measurable claims about hybrid working, attendance or workplace technology. It is essentially an event announcement targeted at the workplace design and commercial interiors community.
